items.title: Coldcard hardware wallet users hit by attack — operational security, not the device, was the weak link
points: Attackers exploited gaps in how victims set up and used their Coldcard hardware wallets (an offline device that stores the private keys controlling your bitcoin), rather than a pure hardware flaw.
Users who followed basic security protocols suffered minimal or no losses; those with inadequate setups were compromised.
Immediate advice for affected users: move funds from any potentially compromised wallet to a newly created one with proper security.
Upgrade from single-device custody to multi-signature (requiring approval from several independent devices before a transaction can execute, so no single point of failure exposes funds).
Audit the full custody chain: where the device was purchased, how firmware (the device's built-in software) was verified, and who had physical access.
Alex Thorn's takeaway: brand reputation matters less than implementation — verified firmware, multisig, and regular security audits do the real work.

items.title: Senate punts Clarity Act vote to September
points: Majority Leader John Thune confirmed no vote on the crypto market structure bill before the August recess, as Democrats hold out.
Sticking points: stablecoin rewards, law enforcement powers, and ethics provisions that could affect President Trump's crypto holdings.
SEC Chair Paul Atkins said the regulator is ready to write crypto rules on its own if legislation stalls, though a future administration could reverse them.

items.title: Bitcoin stuck in 'death cross' despite soft jobs data
points: Bitcoin traded at $64,581, up 0.3% over 24 hours.
The chart remains in a 'death cross' (when the short-term moving average of price falls below the long-term average — typically read as a bearish signal).
A weak July payrolls report cut the odds of a September rate hike, offering some support for risk assets.

items.title: Bitcoin wallet dormant since 2011 moves millions
points: A wallet untouched for roughly 14 years transferred millions of dollars in BTC, a possible sign of long-dormant holders becoming active.

items.title: Tokenized asset deposits nearly triple to $7.4B as DeFi shrinks
points: Deposits into tokenized versions of traditional assets — mainly gold, U.S. Treasuries, and the S&P 500 — reached $7.4 billion.

Spot volumes on decentralized exchanges (platforms for peer-to-peer crypto trading without an intermediary) fell about 70% year-over-year, showing a shift toward regulated, traditional-asset products.

items.title: SEC bought a billion airline records to track travelers
points: Report says the SEC purchased roughly a billion airline passenger records for surveillance of travelers.

issues.subject: What Bitcoiners Can Learn From The Coldcard Hack 🔐

headlines: Coldcard hardware wallet users fell victim to a significant security breach; analysis reveals how the attack unfolded and what victims should do immediately.
Hardware wallet setup and custody practices matter more than the device itself—attackers exploited operational weaknesses, not just technical vulnerabilities.
Alex Thorn breaks down lessons Bitcoiners should apply to protect themselves from similar attacks in the future.

sections.title: The Coldcard Attack: What Happened
points: Attackers targeted Coldcard users through operational security gaps in how victims set up and used their wallets, not purely through hardware flaws.

The breach demonstrates that even reputable hardware wallets require proper custody practices (like multi-signature schemes—spreading control across multiple independent devices so no single point of failure exposes funds) to be truly secure.
Victims who followed basic security protocols suffered minimal or no losses, while those with inadequate setups were compromised.

sections.title: Immediate Actions for Affected Users
points: Move funds immediately from any Coldcard wallet you used with potentially compromised practices to a new wallet with properly implemented security measures.
If you used single-device custody, upgrade to multi-signature setup (requiring approval from multiple independent devices before transactions execute).
Review your entire custody chain: where devices were purchased, how firmware was verified, and who had physical access at any point.

sections.title: Lessons for All Bitcoin Holders
points: Hardware wallet brand matters less than implementation: focus on multi-signature setups and verified firmware updates rather than relying on device reputation alone.
Operational security (how you physically handle and access devices) is equally important as cryptographic security (the math protecting your coins).
Regular security audits of your setup and keeping devices fully updated provide measurable protection against emerging attack vectors.
